newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Sept 96/Feb 2 '97 raw sugar output 854,441T.
newsitem.headline: Manila Sept 96/Feb 2 '97 raw sugar output 854,441T.

text.p: Philippine raw sugar output from September 1, 1996 to February 2, 1997 increased to 854,441 tonnes compared to 756,842 tonnes in the same period in the previous crop year, state-agency Sugar Regulatory Administration said on Friday.
In an earlier interview, SRA chief Wilson Gamboa said he expected Philippine raw sugar output in the current crop year (Sept 1, 1996 to August 31, 1997) at 1.8 million tonnes.
Production in the 1997/1998 crop year is expected to slip to 1.7 million tonnes because of delayed planting by sugar farmers due to the present sugar glut.

Local sugar prices dropped to as low as 488 to 500 pesos per kilo bag early this year as against the 900 pesos at the start of the 1996 due to over importation of cheaper sugar from neighbouring countries.

Gamboa, however, said he expected the glut to "evaporate" in August this year. He also said the Philippines will import at least 500,000 tonnes of sugar from crop year 1997/1998 to fill a projected shortfall.
